scope: Offline, source-identified audit of game reports and already sanitized Chrome traces. No browser or performance test is run.

definitions.quantiles: sorted[floor((n-1)*p)] in derived diagnostics; original report summaries are copied verbatim
definitions.preActive: Before the first request associated with sample zero
definitions.activeStartup: First active request through the request before first frontier >=180
definitions.formal: First frontier >=180 through the request before first frontier >= configured limit
definitions.freshState: Present count changed and logic frontier advanced; actual wrapper-entry interval is an additional observation, not physical scanout

failure.scope: The known assertion is allowlisted; other raw error text remains in the SHA-identified source, not in a new unsanitized stack.

cpuThrottle.scope: openProbe and after-open counters precede CPU throttling; subsequent netplay setup and first game callback use the configured per-side rates.

headedLaunch.scope: Window-mode environment control, not a production code change; proxy, input, audio/context, CPU setup, and native GPU arguments are unchanged.

independentChecks.scope: Offline observations on retained results, not reclassification of harness exit status or proof that later harness gates ran.

independentlyDerivedFormalSummary.scope: Independently derived even for failed harness runs; this does not change a raw failure into a pass.

raf.scope: Actual entry/exit boundaries differ from supplied rAF timestamp and reported C++ work. Raw formal summary is unchanged. All >100 ms rows and right-censored pending requests are retained.

audio.scope: Audio rows lack an absolute first-block performance origin. Relative gaps and zero blocks cannot be assigned to an exact rAF instant.

droppedEventAccounting.scope: When malformed and overflow are zero, the collector source has only the out-of-scope category/metadata rejection path left. This filtering is different from local-capacity loss.

localBudget.scope: The local budget counts only sanitized data already delivered. No local overflow cannot prove the native buffer was not full or that undelivered events would fit.

buffer.limitation: The original full flag only trips at >=1. A persistent 0.996245 plateau does not establish remaining usable capacity; reported eventCount zero does not mean no events.

recomputed.scope: The helper requires every recorded page marker to match, at least two separated markers, one page origin and one renderer thread. A missing stop marker is not repaired by extrapolation.

rawCoverage.limitation: No events is not evidence of idle. Match the retained complete time window to existing rAF requests; a non-reproduced stall is not a repair.

observedData.unknownCounterScope: The raw unknown-name counter is incremented before retention; the first byte-budget rejection may increment it without retaining the event.

extentRelativeToMarkers.scope: Extent-only arithmetic using available marker brackets; NOT a validated active-window mapping or per-frame attribution.

attribution.scope: No missing event is interpreted as idle; unknown event-name hashes are not renamed or reverse guessed.

retainedPositiveObservations.scope: Only retained long X events are mapped. A valid marker calibration permits these positive observations despite local loss; absence, complete coverage, task-body identity and causal repair are not inferred.

limitations: Passing gameplay correctness and failed trace collection remain separate outcomes.
A run without a long active rAF gap does not establish repair of an intermittent stall.
The old 5 s completion timeout can leave partial delivered data; absence of tracingComplete leaves data loss unknown.
A near-full native-buffer plateau is not negated by the old >=1 full flag or by zero local overflow.
Available marker arithmetic only describes observed extent when strict mapping is false; no per-frame causal mapping is produced in that case.
Category presence is not complete temporal coverage. Unknown-name hashes retain timing but do not identify an operation.
These traces lack per-batch arrival clocks; the drain bottleneck cannot be separated into Chrome, transport, Node scheduling, or sanitizer cost.
Headed window geometry and Playwright-emulated focus do not prove an unobscured physical foreground window.
Host aggregate CPU is not single-core utilization or frequency stability; process samples can miss short-lived processes.
Activity from a different run is not imported as evidence for any window in this run.
